name: NCCW Television Championship
epitaph: NCCW's mid-card belt, defended most weeks on the fed's own Saturday Matinee per its 1998 recruitment ad, changing hands eight times (two by forced vacancy) before "Strictly Business" Lew Spectre won it, defended it once on pay-per-view, and held it for over eighteen months without a single loss, forfeiting it only when the promotion folded around him.

name: NCCW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: NCCW's top title from the fed's own 1998 opening bell: "Dominator" Don Cameron became its first-ever World Heavyweight Champion and held it twice more inside the fed's own first year, the belt passing through six further champions across the fed's own dated record before Cameron reclaimed it a final time, undated, and spent the fed's final stretch defending it against a mounting challenge from Lew Spectre.

name: NCCW World Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Limited to wrestlers under 230 pounds and rated by the fed's own FAQ a close second to the World Title: changed hands eight times in fifteen months, twice by forced vacancy (an injury, a departure) and the rest inside the ring, with Superstar's own three separate reigns the title's own throughline.

name: NCCW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Changed hands nine times across the fed's own opening fifteen months, including one team discarding the belts on the same night they won them and a masked team's own mid-reign unmasking, before Coast-to-Coast Connection's second reign closes the fed's own dated record.

name: NCCW International Championship
epitaph: The fed's own secondary heavyweight title, defended more often than the World Titles: "GQ" Geoffrey Quartz won it at the fed's own first dated show, and Purple Pride is its own last recorded champion, winning it eight days before the fed's own record breaks off.
